column1: # rules.tsv - the only thing allowed to call a failure "not a defect".
#   rule-id <TAB> case-regex <TAB> detail-regex <TAB> class <TAB> check-id <TAB> reason
# lib/classify.awk applies a rule to a FAIL/ERROR row only when
#   * case-regex matches the case name, AND
#   * detail-regex matches "case name + detail", AND
#   * check-id is "-" or the check recorded in tests/.out/checks.tsv by
#     slices/s07_harness.sh says "ok" for this very run.
# A rule whose check no longer holds is inert: the rows it used to
# explain fall through to class "triage" and fail the suite again. That
# is what keeps this table from becoming a place to hide regressions.
# classes:  product  the code under test is wrong
#           harness  the project's own test script is wrong
#           tool     an external tool is missing or different on this OS
#           env      machine / config / leftover-state, not the code
#           order    artifact of running a group slice in isolation
# The framework unit groups that build a THixRequest on top of the test
# mock TMockIO. src/hix_request.prg sends ReadHeaders/Drain/PeerAlive/
# lUseSSL to its IO object; the mock implements a smaller set, so the
# group dies with "[EXCEPTION] Message not found" before its first
# assertion. Nothing about HIX is involved - see check mock.io.stale.
unit.mockio.messages
column6: tests/unit/src/hix_test_utils.prg TMockIO does not implement the messages src/hix_request.prg sends to its IO object

column1: # The unit suite looks for curl.exe to run its HTTPS cases and reports a
# FAIL when it cannot find it. On Linux curl.exe does not exist.
unit.ssl.curl.exe
column6: tests/unit looks for curl.exe; its HTTPS cases cannot run on Linux

column1: # webapp/test/test_users_module.sh pins API="http://localhost:9090" and
# never reads TEST_API, so the slice cannot point it at the TLS-only
# server and the script aborts on its own preflight.
wa.users.abort
column6: webapp/test/test_users_module.sh hardcodes its API URL and ignores TEST_API

column1: # webapp/test/test_customer_module.sh authenticates with --cookie (send)
# but never --cookie-jar (save), so the session cookie of a successful
# login is thrown away and every session-dependent case after T09 replays
# the pre-auth session and gets 302.
wa.customer.session
column6: webapp/test/test_customer_module.sh never saves the cookie jar of the authenticated session

column1: # Rows named zbf*/zverify* in users.dbf are written by the project's own
# test scripts; residue in the DBF is residue of previous test runs.
repo.data.residue
column6: the zbf*/zverify* rows are inserted by webapp/test/*.sh, not by the app
